problems.title: Merge three CSV files on the ticker
problems.notebook: acc525/Data Analysis/Data Analysis (Part 4) - CLASS EXERCISE SOLUTIONS.ipynb
problems.prompt:
Three files sit in the working directory: `earnings.csv` (ticker, fpe, eps, revenue), `exchange.csv` (ticker, exchg, exchange, country) and `company_names.csv` (tic, conm, cusip, sic).

Merge them into a single DataFrame `data`: `earnings` with `exchange` on `ticker`, then with `company_names` **after renaming its `tic` column to `ticker`**. Print `data.shape`.
hints: `company = company.rename(columns={'tic': 'ticker'})` makes the third key match.
problems.solution:
import pandas as pd

earnings = pd.read_csv("earnings.csv", parse_dates=["fpe"])
exchange = pd.read_csv("exchange.csv")
company = pd.read_csv("company_names.csv").rename(columns={"tic": "ticker"})

data = pd.merge(earnings, exchange, on="ticker")
data = pd.merge(data, company, on="ticker")
print(data.shape)
problems.tests:
assert len(data) == len(earnings), "every earnings row must find its exchange and name"
assert "conm" in data.columns and "exchange" in data.columns
problems.test_summary: Checks the two merges keep every earnings row and add both extra columns.

problems.title: Concatenate every degrees file
problems.notebook: acc525/Data Analysis/Data Analysis (Part 4) - CLASS EXERCISE SOLUTIONS.ipynb
problems.prompt:
The working directory holds several files whose names start with `degrees-that-pay-back`.

Collect *all* of them with `glob.glob('degrees-that-pay-back*.csv')`, read each one, concatenate them into `df` with a fresh index, and print `df.shape`.
hints: `import glob` then `glob.glob('degrees-that-pay-back*.csv')` lists the matching files.
A list comprehension reads them: `[pd.read_csv(f) for f in files]`.
`pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)` stacks them with a clean index.
problems.solution:
import glob
import pandas as pd

files = glob.glob("degrees-that-pay-back*.csv")
frames = [pd.read_csv(path) for path in files]
df = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)

print(df.shape)
problems.tests:
assert len(files) >= 2, "both degrees files must be found"
assert list(df.index) == list(range(len(df))), "ignore_index=True gives a fresh index"
assert "Major" in df.columns
problems.test_summary: Checks every matching file was found, stacked with a fresh index and readable columns.

problems.title: A left join that keeps the sales rows
problems.notebook: acc525/Data Analysis/Data Analysis (Part 4) - CLASS EXERCISE SOLUTIONS.ipynb
problems.prompt:
`sales` and `spend` are given below. Merge them on **both** `product_id` and `month` with `how='left'` so that every sales row is kept, even where no spend was recorded.

Print how many rows have a missing `spend`.
hints: A missing value after a left join appears as `NaN`, found with `.isna()`.
problems.tests:
assert len(df) == len(sales), f"a left join keeps {len(sales)} rows, got {len(df)}"
assert int(df["spend"].isna().sum()) == 1, f"one row has no spend, got {int(df['spend'].isna().sum())}"
problems.test_summary: Checks the left join keeps every sales row and leaves exactly one spend missing.

problems.title: Export with a pipe delimiter
problems.notebook: acc525/Data Analysis/Data Analysis (Part 4) - CLASS EXERCISE SOLUTIONS.ipynb
problems.prompt:
Fill in the blanks so the DataFrame is written to `mydata.txt` with `|` as the separator and no index column, then read back with `pd.read_csv` using the same separator.

Print the column names of the file you just wrote.
problems.starter_code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"employee": ["Alice", "Bob"], "sales": [12000, 7000]})
df.to_csv("mydata.txt", sep=___, index=___)
back = pd.read_csv("mydata.txt", sep="|")

print(list(back.columns))

blanks.hint: The separator is a pipe character.
The index should not be written.

hints: `index=False` stops pandas writing the row numbers.
problems.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"employee": ["Alice", "Bob"], "sales": [12000, 7000]})
df.to_csv("mydata.txt", sep="|", index=False)
back = pd.read_csv("mydata.txt", sep="|")

print(list(back.columns))
